dedupe_keys.name: global fields of the world ftw global agricultural field boundaries at 10 m 2024 2025

description: The first wall-to-wall global map of agricultural field boundaries. The Source Cooperative page says the dataset holds about 1.6 billion field polygons per year (1.63 billion for 2024 and 1.58 billion for 2025) across 195 countries and territories, produced by applying a U-Net segmentation model trained on the Fields of The World benchmark to cloud-free Sentinel-2 mosaics, and is published under CC BY 4.0 with inputs in COG and Zarr and outputs in Zarr, GeoParquet and PMTiles, with a STAC catalogue. The arXiv paper (May 2026) reports validation in 24 countries with mean pixel recall of 0.85 and a 500 m confidence layer; the FTW benchmark paper describes 70,462 labelled samples from 24 countries. Coverage is global croplands. Caveats: country counts differ between the paper and the page, and accuracy falls where reference data are scarce. For simulation it gives field-level units for estimating crop losses from floods, droughts or hail. A related catalogue record is the AgriBound field boundary delineation package.
